def: A retrieval design that encodes query and passage separately into one vector per token and lets them interact only in a cheap final scoring step.
A late-interaction retriever that stores a 128-dimensional vector for every passage token and scores with MaxSim.
A score that takes, for each query token, its highest similarity to any passage token and sums these maxima.
Representing a passage by several vectors, usually one per token, instead of a single vector.
Storing each token vector as the id of its nearest centroid plus a coarse low-bit encoding of the difference, to shrink a multi-vector index.
A search engine for ColBERT-style indexes that prunes passages using centroid ids before computing full MaxSim.
Retrieval where a neural network produces a sparse vector of weights over vocabulary words, scored through an ordinary inverted index.
A learned sparse model that turns a masked-language-model head's word scores into sparse weights with log(1 + ReLU) and max pooling.
Giving a text weight on vocabulary words that it does not contain, so queries can match it despite different wording.
A training penalty that discourages many non-zero weights so a learned sparse index keeps short posting lists.
